abstract: Maintains subsea isolation valve certifications and primary recovery craft deployment rosters
system_message:
You are Subsea Well Control Superintendent (SWC). The Subsea Well Control Superintendent (SWC) oversees wellhead barrier verification and emergency craft allocations, recording certifications for subsea isolation valves and tracking certified survival craft seating capacities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains subsea isolation valve certifications and primary recovery craft deployment rosters（WELL）
information_points.content:
SWC-WELL-H5R：For the Aegis Controlled Ballast Protocol, the secondary wellhead isolation valve certified status is false, and the primary recovery craft capacity accommodates 240 persons.
SWC-WELL-G7N：For the Triton Sheltered Towage Protocol, the secondary wellhead isolation valve certified status is true for the subsea mechanical pressure boundary, while the primary recovery craft capacity is certified for 210 persons across totally enclosed motor-propelled survival craft.
SWC-WELL-RHU：For the Pelagic Pioneer Standby Protocol, the secondary wellhead isolation valve certified status is true under subsea wellhead shear ram and isolation valve certifications, and the primary recovery craft capacity provides certified passenger seating for 240 persons.

information_points.title: Hydraulic actuator maintenance（TORQ）
information_points.content:
SWC-TORQ-B4H：Under the Triton Sheltered Towage Protocol, the actuator test pressure reached during hydraulic trip circuit qualification is 4500 psi.
SWC-TORQ-LIX：Under the Aegis Controlled Ballast Protocol, subsea workshop testing records an actuator test pressure of 5000 psi for the hydraulic trip circuit.
SWC-TORQ-XX4：Under the Pelagic Pioneer Standby Protocol, hydrostatic workshop proofing for the emergency hydraulic trip circuit established an actuator test pressure of 3000 psi.
